statement.text:
Suppose that H is a subgroup of a finite soluble group G that covers all
Frattini chief factors of G and avoids all complemented chief factors of G. Is it true
that there are elements x, y ∈ G such that H ∩ H x ∩ H y = HG , where HG is the
largest normal subgroup of G contained in H?
    This is true if H is a prefrattini subgroup of G.               S. F. Kamornikov
  ∗ Yes, it is true (S. F. Kamornikov, O. L. Shemetkova, J. Algebra, 641 (2024), 1–8).
